title.description: Short, clear title for the simulation. Should indicate the physics concept. Examples: "Toss Ball", "Two Boxes Collision", "Pendulum Motion"

description.description: Brief educational description for students explaining what they can learn or observe. Keep it engaging.

environment.description: Environment settings. Controls units, scale, boundaries, and gravity. Uses real-world physics coordinates: origin at bottom-left, Y increases upward.

walls.description: Array of walls to include. Options: "left", "right", "top", "bottom". Empty array [] = no walls (objects can exit canvas). Use walls to contain objects or create bounce surfaces.

gravity.description: Gravity acceleration in units/s² (downward). Default: 9.8 for Earth gravity in m/s². Set to 0 for zero-gravity. For cm/s² use 980.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for all positions, velocities, and sizes. Default: "m" (meters). Options: "m", "cm", "km", "ft", "in".

angleUnit.description: Display unit for angle quantities such as "velocity.angle" / "acceleration.angle". Default: "deg". Options: "deg", "rad", "rot". Mirrors `unit` for the angle family; physics is radians internally.

pixelsPerUnit.description: Scale factor: how many pixels equal one unit. The simulation canvas is 800×600 pixels, so the SI canvas size is (800/pixelsPerUnit) × (600/pixelsPerUnit). Pick this value so the largest object is roughly 10–25% of the smaller canvas dimension.

physicsEngine.description: Which physics engine powers the simulation. "rapier" uses Rapier (WASM, SI-native, deterministic, default). "planck" uses Planck.js (pure JS port of Box2D, SI-native). Existing configs without this field use rapier.

airResistance.description: Optional air-resistance configuration. When omitted or .enabled = false, no per-frame drag is applied and bodies move undamped. When .enabled = true, quadratic mass-dependent drag is computed per body each frame from its dragCoefficient · referenceArea and the environment's airDensity.

enabled.description: When true, dynamic objects experience quadratic, mass-dependent drag: F_drag = ½·ρ·Cd·A·|v|·v. Each body uses its dragCoefficient and referenceArea (or shape-based defaults). When false (or omitted), no air-resistance compute runs and bodies move undamped. Default: false.

airDensity.description: Air density ρ in kg/m³. Default: 1.225 (Earth at sea level). Use 0 for vacuum, ~0.020 for Mars surface, ~67 for Venus surface, ~1.977 for cold/dense air. Applies uniformly to every body subject to drag.

objects.description: Array of physics objects in the simulation. 1-3 objects recommended. Each object's collider shape and visual sprite both come from its `svg` manifest entry, scaled to width × height — except container objects, whose sprite and concave collider are synthesized from their `container` parameters.

items.description: A physics object in the simulation. Carries position, bounding-box size, an SVG manifest name (which drives both visual and collider), and optional physics properties.

id.description: Unique identifier for this object (e.g., "ball", "boxA", "platform"). Used by controls, outputs, and graphs to reference this object.

x.description: Initial X position of the object's center, in configured units. With default settings (pixelsPerUnit=10, unit="m"), canvas is 80m wide. X=0 is left edge.

y.description: Initial Y position of the object's center, in configured units. With default settings, canvas is 60m tall. Y=0 is bottom edge, Y increases upward. For container objects with mode "grounded" (the default), ramp objects (always ground-seated), and objects carrying `seatOn`, y is derived at load — author 0 as a placeholder.

width.description: Bounding-box width in configured units. REQUIRED unless `container` or `ramp` is present (then derived from those parameters — omit it). DIORAMA-SIZED, not real-world: pick from the SKELETON's scene_dimension so the largest object is ~10% of the smaller scene dimension and the smallest stays ≥ 4%. A "real" soccer ball is 0.22 m, but at a 30 m scene that's invisible — emit ~3 m instead. The actual collider shape (rectangle, circle, or polygon) is looked up from the SVG manifest by `svg` and scaled into this box.

height.description: Bounding-box height in configured units. REQUIRED unless `container` or `ramp` is present (then derived — omit it). DIORAMA-SIZED, not real-world: pick to match the SVG's natural aspect ratio given `width`. The actual collider shape is looked up from the SVG manifest by `svg` and scaled into this box.

svg.description: Name of a renderable from public/renderables/manifest.json (e.g., "soccer_ball", "brick_block", "boat"). REQUIRED unless `container` is present (then the sprite and collider are synthesized — omit it). Drives both the visual sprite and the physical collider shape, scaled to width × height.

container.description: Open-container synthesis parameters (cup / open box / wagon — a U or L profile that can CATCH and CARRY other bodies). When present, the runtime derives this object's sprite, concave collider, width, height, and svg from these parameters — OMIT width/height/svg on this object. All other physics fields (mass, friction, restitution, velocity, isStatic, showVectors) stay top-level as usual. Container-specific defaults: mass 2, restitution 0.1, friction 0.7 (grounded) / 0.5 (free).

innerWidth.description: Inner cavity width in configured units — the open mouth a payload falls into. Diorama-size it like any object (containers are usually the largest body in the scene) and make it at least 1.5× the payload's width so the catch reads cleanly.

wallHeight.description: Inner depth, floor top to rim, in configured units. Roughly equal to innerWidth for a cup that keeps its catch; smaller for a shallow tray.

wallThickness.description: Wall thickness in configured units. Default: 12% of innerWidth, clamped to a visible diorama minimum. Usually omit.

floorThickness.description: Floor slab thickness in configured units. Default: equal to wall thickness. Usually omit.

walls.description: "both" (default) = U profile (cup / open box). "left" / "right" = keep only that wall (L profile) — e.g. a cart with just a back wall so the payload slides off the open side (Newton's first law demos).

mode.description: "grounded" (default) spawn-seats the container exactly on the floor — requires environment.walls to include "bottom"; the object's authored y is ignored (author y: 0). "free" places the center at the authored (x, y).

fill.description: CSS color for the synthesized sprite's fill. Optional.

stroke.description: CSS color for the synthesized sprite's outline. Optional.

ramp.description: Ramp / inclined-plane synthesis parameters — STATIC environment geometry (a right triangle). When present, the runtime synthesizes this object's sprite and collider and derives width/height/svg and y — OMIT width/height/svg, author y: 0 as a placeholder, and do not emit isStatic (ramps are always static). Give exactly TWO of {angle, rise, run, slopeLength}. Ramps seat on the floor: environment.walls MUST include "bottom". Ramp friction defaults to 0 (frictionless); for friction lessons set the SAME friction value on the ramp AND the object sliding on it (engines use the max of the pair — µ < tan(angle) slides, µ > tan(angle) sticks). Objects start ON the incline via their own `seatOn` field.

angle.description: Incline angle above the horizontal, in the environment angleUnit (default degrees). Give exactly TWO of {angle, rise, run, slopeLength}; the rest are derived. Diorama range ≈ 5–80° (clamped outside it); common teaching values 20–40°.

rise.description: Vertical height of the incline (the h in mgh), in configured units. The most useful second parameter — energy problems and "released from height h" scenarios speak in rise.

run.description: Horizontal base length of the incline, in configured units.

slopeLength.description: Length along the incline surface (the hypotenuse — the d in slide-distance problems), in configured units.

highSide.description: Which side is high. "left" (default): crest at the left, seated objects slide/roll toward +x. "right" mirrors the incline.

fill.description: CSS color for the synthesized sprite's fill. Optional.

stroke.description: CSS color for the synthesized sprite's outline. Optional.

seatOn.description: Id of a `ramp` object to seat this object on at t = 0. The runtime derives this object's y and angle so it rests flush on the incline surface at the authored x — author y: 0 as a placeholder and omit angle (x past the surface span is clamped to the nearest edge). A START POSE only, not an attachment: once the sim runs the object moves freely — it slides down or leaves the ramp under normal physics. Ideal for "block released on an incline" and "ball rolls down a ramp" scenarios.

velocity.description: Initial linear velocity, authored either as components {x, y} or as polar {magnitude, angle} — e.g. a projectile launched at 20 units/s, 45° above horizontal: {"magnitude": 20, "angle": 45}. Components and magnitude are in units/second; angle is in the environment angleUnit (default degrees), counter-clockwise from +X. Positive Y = upward motion. Use ONE form per value — never mix x/y with magnitude/angle. Typical speed range: -30 to 30 m/s (magnitude ≥ 0).

anyOf.description: 2D vector for position, velocity, or acceleration. Coordinate system: origin (0,0) at BOTTOM-LEFT, X increases right, Y increases upward (real-world physics coordinates).

x.description: X component. Positive = rightward, negative = leftward. Applies to position, velocity, and acceleration uniformly. Values are in the simulation's configured units (e.g., meters).

y.description: Y component. Positive = upward, negative = downward (physics convention: Y-up, origin at bottom-left). Applies to position, velocity, and acceleration uniformly. Note: gravity is a separate scalar field with its own sign convention (positive magnitude = downward pull).

anyOf.description: Polar form of a 2D vector: {magnitude, angle}. Interchangeable with the {x, y} component form — normalized to components at load (x = magnitude·cos(angle), y = magnitude·sin(angle)). Author a given value as pure polar OR pure components; never mix fields from both forms.

magnitude.description: Vector length, ≥ 0, in the same units as the equivalent {x, y} components (e.g. units/second for velocity).

angle.description: Direction, measured counter-clockwise from +X, in the environment angleUnit (default degrees). 0 = rightward, 90 (deg) = straight up.

acceleration.description: Additional constant linear acceleration {x, y} in units/s², applied ON TOP OF environment gravity (and any other force acting on the body) each frame via velocity integration (v += a·dt). NOT a gravity override — environment.gravity continues to act on this body. This is a KINEMATIC STIPULATION ("this body accelerates at a"), not a force: its cause is deliberately unmodelled, which is what makes it the right tool for KINEMATICS-chapter sims, where constant acceleration is taught before Newton's laws and owes no force story. Use for non-gravity constant accelerations: rocket thrust ({x:0, y:15}), constant braking deceleration ({x:-3, y:0} on a body moving +x), conveyor-belt push, a constant horizontal wind, etc. Leave unset (or {x:0, y:0}) for plain gravity-only motion. Typical range: -20 to 20 m/s². CAUTION — in a DYNAMICS scene (friction, air resistance, or an applied force on the same body) this acceleration still moves the body and still appears in "force-net" as m·a, but NO force arrow accounts for it, so a free-body diagram cannot close. If the lesson is that something PUSHES the body, author that force instead. The runtime reports this mixed-chapter case on the diagnostics bus.

x.description: X component. Positive = rightward, negative = leftward. Applies to position, velocity, and acceleration uniformly. Values are in the simulation's configured units (e.g., meters).

y.description: Y component. Positive = upward, negative = downward (physics convention: Y-up, origin at bottom-left). Applies to position, velocity, and acceleration uniformly. Note: gravity is a separate scalar field with its own sign convention (positive magnitude = downward pull).

restitution.description: Bounciness (0-1). 0 = no bounce, 1 = perfect bounce, 0.8 = realistic. Default: 0.8

friction.description: Surface friction (0-1). Affects sliding against other objects. Default: 0.1

dragCoefficient.description: Dimensionless drag coefficient (Cd) for the per-frame quadratic air-resistance model. Examples: 0.47 (sphere), 1.05 (cube broadside), 1.28 (flat plate), 1.5 (parachute / feather, high-drag). Set to 0 to opt this body out of air resistance entirely. Defaults to a shape-based value (sphere=0.47, rectangle=1.05, polygon=1.0). Active only when environment.airResistance.enabled is true.

referenceArea.description: Drag reference area in m² for the per-frame quadratic air-resistance model. Defaults to the body's widest horizontal extent (treating the 2D world as a 1m-deep slice) — a stand-in for projected area perpendicular to vertical motion, the dominant case in secondary-curriculum drag problems. Override explicitly when the body travels horizontally (set to vertical extent instead) or when the body's shape implies a non-default frontal area. See the in-app "Design philosophy" doc for the linear-A scoping rationale.

inertia.description: inertia is the second moment of area in two dimensions, affects rotation. Set to 1e10 for to prevent body rotation. Default: 0

isStatic.description: If true, object is immovable (good for floors, walls, platforms). Default: false

mass.description: Mass of the object in kg. Default: 1

angularVelocity.description: Initial angular velocity in radians/second. Default: 0

showVectors.description: Vector arrows to draw on this object. Each entry is either a shorthand kind string ("velocity", "acceleration", "force-net", "force-applied", "force-friction", "force-drag", "force-gravity") for default styling, or a full {kind, color?, label?, labelPlacement?, labelFontSize?, pixelsPerUnit?} config for per-arrow overrides. Multiple kinds can be combined on one body (e.g., ["velocity", "acceleration"] for a projectile, ["force-applied", "force-friction", "force-net"] for a Newton's 2nd Law diorama). Default: no arrows. (Legacy `showForceArrows: true` is auto-translated to `showVectors: ["force-net"]`.)

items.description: Either a kind name shorthand ("velocity") for default styling, or a full {kind, color?, label?, ...} config for per-arrow overrides.

anyOf.description: Vector arrow kind. Drives default color, scale, and label. "velocity" reads body.velocity; "acceleration" reads finite-differenced total acceleration; "force-net" = m·a_derived; the remaining force kinds are wired by later phases.
A single vector arrow rendered on an object, with optional per-arrow visual overrides.

kind.description: Vector arrow kind. Drives default color, scale, and label. "velocity" reads body.velocity; "acceleration" reads finite-differenced total acceleration; "force-net" = m·a_derived; the remaining force kinds are wired by later phases.

components.description: When true, draw this vector decomposed into its two axis-aligned component arrows (e.g. vₓ horizontal and v_y vertical) instead of the single resultant arrow. Both legs originate at the object. The full resultant is NOT drawn — to show it alongside the components, add the plain kind as a separate entry, e.g. ["velocity", {"kind": "velocity", "components": true}]. Ideal for projectile motion (constant vₓ, ramping v_y). Decomposition is along horizontal/vertical; a rotated basis (incline plane) is not yet supported.

pixelsPerUnit.description: Override the kind's default pixels-per-SI-unit scale.

color.description: Override the kind's standard color (any CSS color string).

label.description: Override the kind's standard label. A plain string is rendered as-is; {main, sub} renders the sub as a subscript; `null` suppresses the label entirely.

sub.description: Subscript (e.g., "net", "app", "ar"). Rendered smaller with a baseline shift.

labelPlacement.description: Where to anchor the label relative to the arrow. Default: "midpoint" with a perpendicular offset to the arrow's left.

labelFontSize.description: Override the default label font size in px.

controls.description: Interactive controls (sliders, toggles) for students to adjust parameters. Include at least one for interactivity.

items.description: Interactive control for students to adjust simulation parameters. Sliders for numeric values, toggles for booleans.

oneOf.description: Slider control for adjusting numeric properties. Values are in real-world units (meters, etc.) with Y-up coordinates.

label.description: Display label shown to users (e.g., "Initial Velocity", "Box A Speed")

targetObj.description: ID of the object to control (must match an object's id)

property.description: Property path to control. Cartesian components: "velocity.x", "velocity.y", "position.x", "position.y", "acceleration.x", "acceleration.y". Polar projections: "velocity.magnitude" / "velocity.angle" (and the same for acceleration). A ".magnitude" slider changes speed while preserving direction; an ".angle" slider rotates the vector while preserving magnitude — ideal for projectile launch (a Speed slider + a Launch-angle slider). Angle is in the environment's angleUnit (default degrees), measured counter-clockwise from +X. Scalars: "mass", "restitution", "friction", "angle", "isStatic". Ramp-dimension paths (target must be a `ramp` object): "ramp.angle", "ramp.rise", "ramp.run", "ramp.slopeLength" — the slider overrides that synthesis param and the incline rebuilds live (seated riders re-seat automatically); the overridden param's companion is the first-authored remaining param, so author {angle, slopeLength} for a tilt-a-fixed-board angle slider (the classic tilt-until-slip friction demo). Note: an "acceleration.*" slider drives an ADDITIONAL constant acceleration on top of environment gravity (rocket thrust, braking, conveyor push) — not a gravity override.

min.description: Minimum slider value in configured units. Velocity: typically -30 to 30 m/s. Position X: 0 to canvas width. Position Y: 0 to canvas height. Acceleration: typically -20 to 20 m/s² for non-gravity effects.

max.description: Maximum slider value in configured units. With default settings: Position X max ~80m, Position Y max ~60m.

step.description: Slider increment in configured units. Use 0.01 for fine control, 0.1 for coarse control.

defaultValue.description: Initial value when simulation loads in configured units. Should match the object's initial property value.

targetObj.description: ID of the object to control (must match an object's id)

outputs.description: Real-time value displays. Group by object. Show velocity, acceleration, position as relevant.

items.description: A group of output values, typically for one object. Groups values visually.

values.description: Array of values to display in this group

items.description: A single value to display in real-time. Values are automatically converted to real-world units.

targetObj.description: ID of the object to read from (must match an object's id)

property.description: Property path to display. Cartesian components: "velocity.x", "velocity.y", "acceleration.x", "acceleration.y", "position.x", "position.y". Polar projections: "velocity.magnitude" (speed, |v|), "velocity.angle" (direction), and the same for acceleration. Magnitude is in the configured length unit; angle is in the environment angleUnit (default degrees), counter-clockwise from +X.

unit.description: Unit label for display (e.g., "m/s", "m/s²", "m"). Will use the configured unit type. Leave blank to auto-generate based on property and environment unit.

graphs.description: Time-series graphs to visualize property changes. Great for comparing related quantities.

items.description: Graph configuration. Currently supports line graphs for time-series data.

oneOf.description: Time-series line graph. X-axis is time, Y-axis shows property values in real-world units. Great for comparing velocity vs acceleration.

title.description: Graph title (e.g., "Velocity Over Time", "Position vs Time")

yAxisRange.description: Y-axis range in configured units. X-axis is always time in seconds.

min.description: Minimum Y-axis value in configured units (e.g., -2 for -2 m/s). Set to encompass expected values with padding.

max.description: Maximum Y-axis value in configured units (e.g., 2 for 2 m/s). Set to encompass expected values with padding.

yAxisLabel.description: Y-axis label with units (e.g., "Velocity (m/s)", "Position (m)"). If not provided, defaults to "Value".

lines.description: Array of lines to plot. Use contrasting colors for multiple lines.

items.description: Configuration for a single line on a graph. Values are automatically converted to real-world units.

label.description: Line label for the legend (e.g., "Velocity Y", "Box A Position")

targetObj.description: ID of the object to track (must match an object's id)

property.description: Property path to plot. Cartesian components: "velocity.x", "velocity.y", "acceleration.x", "acceleration.y", "position.x", "position.y". Polar projections: "velocity.magnitude" (speed), "velocity.angle" (direction), and the same for acceleration. Overlaying e.g. ["velocity.x", "velocity.y", "velocity.magnitude"] is a useful component-vs-resultant view. Magnitude is in the configured length unit; angle is in the environment angleUnit (default degrees), counter-clockwise from +X.
